citation.authors: Rubio C, Napoleone G, Luis-Gonzalez G et al

cited_by.title: Sea moss (Irish moss): health claims, iodine and heavy metals

record.population: Edible seaweed samples (Chondrus, Eisenia, Gelidium, Himanthalia, Laminaria, Palmaria, Porphyra, Undaria) from Asia and the EU
record.design: Laboratory analysis of 20 metals by ICP-OES
record.finding: Red seaweed showed higher concentrations of trace and toxic elements. At 4 g a day of seaweed the intake of aluminium, cadmium and lead was low and the authors saw no serious concern, but they say other toxic metals should be monitored.
record.note: Lab analysis of dried seaweed products, not of sea moss gel or drinks, and not of people. The authors' 4 g a day is a small dried amount.
